emily.title: Username
emily.text:
Emily asks you to meet her on the bridge over the canal after close. She's there before you. She's twisting the strap of her satchel in both hands, and the lamplight is shivering on the water below.

She has plainly rehearsed this. She has just as plainly forgotten every word.

"Okay. So. This is going to sound insane." She takes a breath. "I told you there was something I had to say, and that I wasn't brave enough yet. I'm still not. I'm doing it anyway."

Then she says your old forum username out loud.

Nobody in this world should know it. You haven't heard it spoken in your life. You only ever saw it typed, in a little grey box, next to a wolf-girl's avatar.

Her ears are flat against her hair. Her tail is wrapped around her own leg.

"Please tell me I didn't just say a random string of letters to a stranger," she whispers. "Please. I have been carrying that for a year."
ngpp: She grips your sleeve, and for a second she stops and looks down at the ripples on the canal. Something crosses her face. She has the odd feeling she has stood on this bridge before, saying these same words. She shakes her head and the feeling goes.

"Wait." She frowns at the cobblestones. "I remember six years of threads from my dorm, Sam. So why does this bridge feel like a scene we already played? I know where you'll stand before you move." Her ears twitch. You step to exactly that spot.

"Don't laugh, Shadowkin," Emily says, and leans against your sleeve before you've offered it. "I know this is the first time on paper. It isn't the first time for my tail. It knows how fast you walk across this bridge." She says it flatly, like a fact she checked.

choices.label: Say "Shadowkin?"
choices.res: She makes a noise you have only ever seen typed as a keysmash. Then she grabs your sleeve with both hands and holds on. Her tail thumps the bridge stones, and her glasses slip down her nose, and she doesn't fix them. "It's really you," she says into your coat. "It's really, actually you." The lamp oil runs low before she lets go.

choices.label: "You still owe me the end of that campaign."
choices.res: "It was YOUR turn to post!" she says, outraged, and her ears snap upright. Then her face crumples. She is crying and laughing at the same time, and she has to take off her glasses to wipe them on her sleeve. "Six years. A year here. And you pick now to bring up the campaign." She leans on your shoulder anyway.

image.comp: standing on a canal bridge at night, hands clasped, wolf ears flat, glasses, hopeful and terrified smile
image.setting: stone bridge over a canal, lamplight on the water

emily.title: Bath Lag
emily.text:
You open the washroom door, and Emily is in the tub.

She has a notebook balanced on the rim. Her glasses are fogged, and one damp wolf ear has flopped sideways. She's muttering to herself in a low, gravelly voice.

You know the voice. You read it for six years. It's the narrator she used for her character, the one who always opened a scene.

"And then the wolf drew her blade, and she said..."

She looks up.

Her tail slaps the water and soaks the edge of the notebook. She snatches it up and holds it against her chest. It doesn't cover very much.

"I was drafting dialogue," she says. She's mortified. "Out loud. In the bath. Like a normal person." She pushes her glasses up and they fog again at once. "I always did it out loud. You just couldn't hear me, because I was typing. Oh no. You know what I sound like now."

1.title: Reconnecting in Steam
1.text:
You push open the washroom door. Emily is rinsing foam off one fluffy wolf ear, with her glasses pushed up on top of her head.

She doesn't drop anything this time. She blinks at you through the steam, goes pink, and slides along the bench. She pats the space next to her tail.

"Oh. Hi, Sam. Um." She points at her own head. "I can never get the soap out from behind my ears. They're a design flaw. Would you?" Her tail has started to wag, slowly, and she glances at it and gives up. "That's an out-of-character request, by the way. That one's just from me."

choices.label: Kneel beside the tub and brush gently behind her wolf ears
choices.res: Her ears twitch hard when your thumbs find the base of them, then flatten and go limp. The soap runs down her neck. She makes a small, helpless sound and leans back into your chest. Then she twists around, fogged glasses forgotten, and kisses you. It is clumsy and wet and she doesn't stop for a while.
choices.fallbackRes: You rinse the soap from behind her ears and she melts against your palms. Her tail flops over your knee and stays there. She whispers that nobody has ever done that, and that she'd like you to keep doing it, and you keep doing it until the water goes cool.

choices.label: Rescue her notebook from the spray and wish her luck writing
choices.res: You lift the notebook off the wet rim before the next splash gets it, and she looks at you like you've pulled someone out of a river. "Hero," she says. You put it on the dry towel rack. She tells you the scene she was drafting, quietly, with her ears pink, and you stay on the bench and listen to the end of it.

3.title: No Narrator Needed
3.text:
There's no notebook on the rim tonight.

Emily is sitting in the steaming water, naked, with her grey tail curled around one ankle and her glasses already on the towel shelf. She's blushing to the tips of her ears. Her nipples are stiff, and she isn't hiding them. She holds both hands out toward the front of your shirt.

"The server's private, Sam." Her voice wobbles and then steadies. "Lock the door and climb in. I've written this scene about forty times and deleted it. I want to find out what actually happens when you fuck me."

choices.label: Slip naked into the hot water with her
choices.res: You strip, and she watches every button with her lip between her teeth. The water is hot around your legs as you climb in. Emily squeaks, then laughs at herself, and her wet tail curls around your waist to pull you closer. Her hands are on your chest and her face is flushed. "Okay," she breathes. "Okay. Here we go."

choices.label: Kiss down her wet collarbones slowly in the steam
choices.res: You sit on the edge of the tub and kiss her collarbone, then lower, slowly, through the steam. Her breath catches. She grips the cedar rim and her ears quiver. She starts to say your name and gives up halfway. Every sound she used to spend paragraphs hiding comes out of her now, and she lets it.

choices.label: Apologize and back out
choices.res: "It's fine!" she squeaks, from somewhere behind the notebook, and you shut the door and stand in the hallway with your face hot. You hear a lot of splashing. That evening a note slides under your door. It says brb dying of embarrassment, and it's signed with a tiny wolf doodle chewing its own tail.

choices.label: Answer in your old character's voice
choices.res: You answer in the voice of your old character, the bard, with a flourish nobody can see. There is a long silence. Then she answers back, in character, and the two of you play the whole scene through the door, you facing the hallway. She laughs so hard the water sloshes, and the narrator voice cracks completely.

choices.label: Stand there, flustered
choices.res: Her ears go flat. "Lag," she whispers, clutching the notebook. "You're lagging. Please reconnect." You open your mouth and nothing useful comes out. You try again and fail again. She starts giggling into her hands, and then her glasses slip off her nose and drop into the water with a small plop.

image.comp: in a tub with a notebook on the rim, fogged glasses, wolf ears perked up in surprise, tail splashing

emily.title: Session Zero
emily.text:
Emily talks you into running the campaign again. It will be on paper this time, in the lounge after close.

She has prepared. She's carved dice out of wooden cubes and inked the pips herself. She's written out character sheets for both of you, with the tidy headers she always used on the forum. She sets out snacks in labeled bowls, and her tail sweeps the rug while she does it.

It's the same story. You left it in the middle of a scene, years ago, when your account went quiet. Her wolf and your bard were standing outside a locked door. She has remembered exactly where everyone was.

The fire pops. You roll, and you narrate. It comes back as if it had never gone.

Then, halfway through the session, her character turns to yours and says something. It isn't in any of the old logs. It's not the sort of thing her wolf ever said.

Emily has stopped looking at her sheet. She's looking at you over the top of it.

choices.label: Take it OOC on the hearth rug
choices.res: You roll the wooden dice out of reach and take the character sheet from her trembling hands. She doesn't object. You pull her down beside you on the hearth rug, and the fire is warm on her cheek. She's breathing fast, and her tail thumps against your calves. "Is this in character?" she whispers. "No," you say. She kisses you first.

choices.label: Answer in character
choices.res: You answer in character, in your bard's voice, with the line she hoped you'd pick. She drops a die and picks it up. She drops it again. Finally she hides behind her character sheet with only the tips of her ears showing, and they are quivering. "That was in the notes," she says, muffled. "I didn't think you'd read the notes."

choices.label: Ask, out of character, if she meant it
choices.res: "OOC?" she says, very small, and her ears dip behind the paper. The fire pops. She lowers the sheet an inch. "Yeah. OOC, I meant it. I've meant it for a while." She turns a die over in her fingers and doesn't look at it. The game sits forgotten between you, and neither of you reaches to restart it.

image.comp: sitting cross-legged on a sofa with hand-drawn character sheets and wooden dice, peeking over a sheet with a shy smile, tail swishing
image.setting: cozy lounge after close, fireplace glow

emily.title: Last Seen
emily.text:
Emily shows you a page of her notebook. On it, copied out from memory, is the last thing she ever sent you on the forum.

It's two words. "you there?"

It was never answered. The pencil has smudged, because her thumb has been over it for months.

"I kept checking for three weeks," she says quietly. Her ears have drooped. "I'd refresh it between lectures. It said you were last seen on the Tuesday. Then it kept saying that." She closes the notebook and holds it shut. "I didn't know you'd died. I thought I'd done something. I went back through the whole thread, looking for what I'd said wrong."

She pulls her sleeves down over her hands.

"Then I woke up here. And sometimes I think, if I fall asleep the wrong way, I'll wake up back in my dorm, and it'll still say 'last seen', and it'll say that forever."
ngpp: She points to the pencil smudge and then stops, her finger in the air. For a moment she looks as if she has already written your answer under that line. She frowns at the page, then at you, and shakes it off with a small laugh.

"Wait." Her voice goes thin. "I remember every exam week on that forum, Sam. So why does holding this page out feel like something I've done in this exact lounge, in this chair, with you next to me?" She has gone pale. She doesn't take the page back.

Emily puts her pencil into your hand before you ask. "I remember Earth," she says, steady now. "I also remember this room, and this page, and your handwriting going right under that line. I don't know how. I'm sure of it, though. I'm not guessing."

choices.label: "I'm here."
choices.res: She looks at your face like a chat window, waiting for the typing indicator. It doesn't need to appear. You are here and you are answering. She nods slowly and takes your sleeve in her fist. She holds on for a long time, long after she has stopped needing proof, just to be sure it's real.

choices.label: Write the reply under it
choices.res: You take her pencil and write under her line: yeah. sorry for the lag. Her breath stops. She reads it twice, then presses the notebook to her chest, and her tail thumps once against the chair. She laughs, and the laugh is wet, and she says the reply is three months late and the best she's ever had.

choices.label: "Let's not think about it."
choices.res: "Right. Sure." Her ears droop and her tail goes still. She says nothing else. She sits by the fire with the notebook and rereads it alone for the rest of the evening, and it stays dry only because she tries very hard. When you leave she doesn't look up, and the page is still open.

image.comp: holding an open notebook toward him, ears drooped, tail low, glasses, fear in her eyes

emily.title: New Constellations
emily.text:
Under a full moon, Emily takes you up onto the roof with a blanket and her notebook.

None of the stars here match the ones at home. She checked for the first few months, and she kept a list. Then she gave up and started naming them herself.

She's named them after the campaign. She shows you, pointing with her pencil. There's the Cursed Lute. There's the Bard Who Never Posted, which she says is a joke, mostly. There's a long crooked one near the horizon that she has called the Wolf and the Idiot.

"You're the idiot," she adds. "In case that wasn't clear."

Her ears and her tail have relaxed. She's lying back on the slates in the silver light. She's at ease, and you don't think she's noticed.

"I figured, if we're stuck here, we ought to have our own sky at least," she says. "I spent a year looking up at somebody else's. It's much better with you in it."

choices.label: Name one together
choices.res: You argue happily for an hour over a single cluster of stars. She wants a name from the campaign. You want one that's rude. You settle on The Streak, and she writes it into the notebook in her best forum-header lettering. Her tail wags the blanket into a heap, and she has to stop writing to fix it, and she doesn't mind.

choices.label: Ask which one is her
choices.res: She points to two stars close together, low in the east, and says nothing. You wait. She doesn't explain, and after a moment she tucks her ears under your chin, the way a cat would, and keeps them there. The stars are still above you. She hasn't said which one is you. She doesn't have to, and you don't ask.

image.comp: lying on a blanket on a rooftop in moonlight pointing at the stars, notebook open, wolf ears relaxed, glancing at him with soft eyes
image.setting: slate rooftop under a full moon, a lantern beside her

emily.title: More Than a Username
emily.text:
Emily stops in the doorway of your room with her notebook hugged against her chest. Her tail is wrapped around her own ankle.

"For six years you were a username," she says. "You were my favorite one. I'd see it light up and my whole evening would get better. I never wanted more than that. I told myself so all the time, because it was true, and because we'd never even heard each other's voices."

She's trembling. Her ears are flat.

"Then I got a whole person. He apologizes to chairs, and he gave me a job before he'd seen my handwriting. And it turns out I do want more. I want all of it." She swallows. "I'm bad at saying things out loud. I've written this down four times, and it was better on paper. So here's the short version."

She takes your hand. Her grip is much surer than her voice.

"Stay online, Sam."

The door closes behind you both.
ngpp: The latch clicks, and her ears twitch. She says "stay online" and then pauses, as if the words are older than the doorway. She glances at the frame and back at you, puzzled, and tightens her grip on your hand.

"I know Earth's dorms line by line, Sam," she says against your shirt. "So why does standing in this doorway feel like logging back in? I've been here. I've said this. I just can't remember the part where it ends." She holds on tighter and waits for you to answer.

"Reset the thread as often as the sky wants," Emily says against your lips, and her tail wraps behind your calf. "I don't care. I know this door. I know you. My account only pairs with yours, and I'm not asking for permission this time. I'm telling you."
emily.goLead: Emily sets her worn notebook down on the dresser and pulls off her glasses. Then she launches herself into your arms and takes you both down onto the bed, ears pinned back and tail thumping.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Emily nods, and her ears wobble, and she holds the notebook tight against her chest. "Okay. I can wait," she says. "I've waited longer for less." She smiles, and it nearly holds. "Just don't go idle on me. I'd notice. I always notice when you go quiet." She squeezes your hand once and lets go.
